question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=AC\), and \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\), meeting \(BC\) at \(D\). The criterion for proving \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ACD\) is:

solutions.explanation: \(AB=AC\), \(\angle BAD=\angle CAD\) (angle bisector), and \(AD=AD\) (common side). Two sides and their included angle are respectively equal, so use SAS.
solutions.title: Use the angle bisector and common side
